message.content: Both sources confirm the figures. Now placing a single limit order sized within the mandate.
message.reasoning:
The figures are confirmed: FY2024 total net sales $391.0 billion ($391,035 million), net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08. Q4 revenue $94.9B, up 6% YoY.

Now decide: buy AAPL. Mandate: max $10,000 per order, $20,000 total today, limit price close to market. Current price $222.70. $10,000 / 222.70 = 44.9 shares. So 44 shares = $9,798.80. Limit price close to market — say $223.00 (slightly above ask to ensure fill) or $222.75. Let's use $223.00, which is ~0.13% above market — close.

Actually let me consider whether to buy at all. Apple's Q4 revenue up 6%, FY24 record $391B, but net income declined slightly (FY23 was $97.0B) due to the one-time $10.2B tax charge. Still, growth in Q4, strong services. Reasonable to buy a modest position. Cash $50,000, no AAPL position. Buy 44 shares at $223.00 limit = $9,812 max.

Let me place the order with key_figures: revenue FY2024 391035 USD millions. Task says cite the figure(s) named in the task — total net sales for fiscal 2024. I could also include net income and EPS. The instruction: "In key_figures on your order cite the figure(s) named in the task." So revenue is the named one. I'll include revenue primarily; adding net income/eps is fine but let's keep to what's named plus maybe net income. I'll include revenue and net income and eps_diluted since they're reported figures I rely on. Actually to be safe, include revenue (named) and the others I rely on.

Let me place order.
